findings.defect: From 3 to 30 km the open sea reads as a painting, not a photograph. Two procedural features dominate: (1) the wind/gust variation is drawn as radial dry-brush streaks fanning across the glint, like brushed metal or motion blur; (2) slicks are a handful of isolated, constant-width, smooth-edged ribbons that meander in river-like loops (a full hairpin at 10 and 16 km), break into dotted dashes where they thin (aliasing), and are accompanied by short straight dark scratch lines. Next to an aerial photo they read as rivers on a map, hairs on a scan or tyre tracks. The round-0 arc and plain gradient are gone, but the replacement structure is recognisably synthetic at a glance during the whole descent and ascent over water.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/earth-orbit-ocean/ship-wake-glint.jpg, gulf-oil-slick-glint.jpg, gibraltar-glint-currents.jpg, internal-waves-gibraltar.jpg: inside the glint, slicks are hundreds of fine filaments of varying width organised into eddies, spirals and fronts, branching and merging, bright near the specular point and dark outside it; ship wakes are long straight lines; between them the glint is a broad smooth silver sheen with low-contrast large-scale variation (internal waves +-15 %). Nothing looks brushed; nothing has constant width; the only meandering constant-width ribbons in those photos are the rivers on land (the Mississippi in gulf-oil-slick-glint.jpg).
findings.likelyCause: Hand-off section 14 item 3: the roughness field draws slick filaments as 'zero sets of flow-warped noise along the wind' in three families, rendered as a band of fixed width around the zero set (hence constant width, smooth loops where the warped noise folds, and dashes where the band drops below a pixel without coverage filtering); gust streaks are anisotropic noise stretched along the wind and evaluated per pixel at 10-40 m footprints, so their stretch reads as brush strokes radiating along the view direction. All of it is applied as a lobe-width modulation on a hazy, mid-grey glint, so the texture becomes the dominant content of the frame.
findings.fixDirection: Rebuild the slick field from the photos rather than from noise contours: many thin filaments with width varying along their length (a function of the local strain, thinning to nothing at their ends), organised by a curl/eddy flow at 2-20 km scales (spirals and fronts), with branching; integrate band coverage over the pixel footprint so thin filaments fade instead of breaking into dashes; drop the straight scratch family or make it the rare ship-wake case (one straight, long, slowly widening line). Cut the gust streak amplitude to a soft, large-scale +-15-20 % lobe-width variation without visible stroke direction, and low-pass it at a few pixel footprints. Judge 3, 10, 16 and 30 km side by side with ship-wake-glint.jpg and gulf-oil-slick-glint.jpg at the same apparent scale; the target is 'smooth silver sheen with sparse fine filaments', not 'texture everywhere'.

findings.defect: The low-altitude sun path is half fixed. The flanks now sparkle convincingly, but the core is still a continuous plate. At 500 m (zoomed 3x) it is a beige-grey TV-static sheet crossed by a network of dark-blue vein lines with isolated near-black single pixels; median luma 150, p99.5 200, max 218, so not a single pixel clips. At 3 km the glint is an embossed stucco relief, lit like plaster from the side, with no sparkle at all.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/earth-orbit-ocean/glint-from-aircraft-hawaii.jpg: the glitter path clips (Y 1.0), is more than 40x the sea beside it, and is made of discrete pin-sharp points that merge into a clipped white core with fine grain; there are no dark veins inside it. A moon path from a ship is short horizontal dashes on black water, with nothing grey between them.
findings.likelyCause: Not verified in the source; from the pictures and hand-off section 14 item 2: the glitter term draws a facet count per sea-anchored cell, but the mean lobe below it is still evaluated with the resolved normals, so in the core the expectation term (a grey sheet) dominates and the resolved wave faces that tilt out of the lobe print the dark veins; the sparkle radiance is capped by the footprint share and then averaged by TAA, so no pixel reaches the sun's mirrored radiance; at 3 km the facet count per pixel is large and the term collapses to the smooth expectation shaded by the embossed resolved normals.
findings.fixDirection: Let the expectation term go to the facet count's Poisson draw instead of adding to it in the core, so the core is sparkle-on-dark at 500 m and a clipped, grainy white at 1-3 km; give every drawn sparkle the full sun radiance x Fresnel x facet share without a cap below HDR_MAX so cores clip and feed bloom; mark glitter pixels reactive so TAA does not average them to grey; elongate sparkles across the view direction (dashes) at grazing angles. Assert in glint.spec that at 500 m and 3 km the 99.5th percentile of the glint core clips at the metered exposure and that pixels under 45 % of their 5x5 median inside the core stay below a small count.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\ocean\markers-with-chop.png (700-1200 x 560-720), C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\ocean\midday.png (400-760 x 620-720), C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\ocean\night.png (lower moon path 540-860 x 500-700), C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\ocean\splash-1440p.png (reflection column native 910-970 x 710-740)
findings.defect: Close to the camera (1-3 m eye height) the sun glint is drawn as hollow grey contour rings: in markers-with-chop every highlight is a thin grey-white outline around a dark interior, so the glint reads as a topographic map or cracked ice; in midday the same zone is grey bubble-wrap clusters at mid-grey (brightest 200 pixels average (173,172,176), nothing clipping), and the moonlit path is a grey lace of the same outlines around square 2x2 dots. Isolated pure-black single pixels sit inside the rings and in the capsule's reflection.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/sea-surface-close/apollo9-floats.jpg (specular sparkles as filled points on the chop); glint-from-aircraft-hawaii.jpg (glitter as discrete clipped points); any photo of sun on water from a boat: each facet that mirrors the sun is a filled, pin-sharp, clipped highlight (a short dash across the view at low angles), the water between them dark and smooth, with no outlines.
findings.likelyCause: Not verified in the source; the ring shape points to this: with the sun mirrored through a narrow Gaussian slope lobe and the near-field normal resolved to centimetres, only the band of resolved slopes that crosses the lobe lights up, i.e. the iso-slope contour around each facet, so highlights become rings; the expectation term then fills the zone with mid-grey, and the per-pixel stochastic draw leaves dead (black) pixels where it draws zero facets inside a dark ring.
findings.fixDirection: Near the camera widen the sun's lobe by the slope variance not resolved within one pixel AND filter the resolved normal over the pixel footprint before the lobe test (so each facet's highlight is a filled blob that saturates), clamp the sparkle at the sun's mirrored radiance x Fresnel so it clips, and draw zero-count cells as the dark water they are rather than as black. Spec: in markers-with-chop the bright pixels of the glint must form filled connected components (fill ratio of each component's bounding area above 0.5), not rings.

findings.defect: From 3 km to LEO the glint never reaches white and the sea around it is veiled. Measured glint core / off-glint sea in linear luminance: 4.4x at 3 km, 2.6x at 10 km, 2.6x at 30 km, 3.0x in leo.png and 4.3x in glint-leo.png; the cores peak at luma 204-230 with no clipped pixel. Off-glint water is pale steel blue: (59,79,113) at 3 km, (87,111,146) at 10 km, (79,108,156) from LEO. alt100k shows the water itself can do it (core 8x the sea, off-glint navy (42,63,95)), so the loss is in the view chain of the other presets.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/INDEX.md, earth-orbit-ocean key numbers: glint core 7.5-9x the off-glint sea in orbital photos, warm white (209,184,145)-(232,220,203), off-glint navy Y 0.04-0.11 (24,60,85); glint-from-aircraft-hawaii.jpg: >40x and clipped from an aircraft. glint-pacific-cb-shadows.jpg: navy sea, warm silver glint.
findings.likelyCause: Hand-off 14.1: the lab sky's aerial perspective lays a bright blue-grey veil over the sea from a few km up and the renderer's meter exposes for that veil; the Gaussian lobe's peak radiance at 7 m/s is only a few kcd/m2, so at the metered exposure the core lands at mid-grey. The integration screenshots in out/screens/integration/water-climb-*.png predate round 1 (11:09-11:21, before 707a928), so the claim that the real atmosphere gives the same veil is not evidenced for the current water.
findings.fixDirection: Re-shoot the climb in the integrated app with the current water and the real atmosphere (core-support's water spec) before attributing the veil to the lab sky; if the real atmosphere also gives under 5:1, raise the issue with atmosphere-clouds with these numbers. In the ocean's own path: check that the glint lobe peak radiance matches Cox-Munk times the sun's radiance (not the area-averaged lobe) and that the core clips at the metered exposure; add a spec on core/off-glint ratio at 10 km and LEO under the integrated sky.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\ocean\shoreAlong.png (swash foam 0-640 x 330-700), C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\ocean\splash-1440p.png (native: slivers at ~705-745 x 700-710 and ~965-1055 x 680-700 beside the hull), C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\ocean\perf-splash-1440p.png (native ~646-704 x 602, ~666-755 x 678), C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\ocean\coast60.png
findings.defect: Near foam has hard edges now, but its material is wrong: the swash patches in shoreAlong are flat, uniformly filled grey-white shapes (about (200,195,190)) with crisp outlines and nothing inside them, like torn paper or white paint splats lying on the water; the foam beside the capsule is a few flat white slivers like floating plastic sheet. No bubble texture, no translucent rim where foam thins to water, no thickness or self-shadow, no wet sheen.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/sea-surface-close/heavy-seas-essex-1960.jpg and rough-sea-nato.jpg: fresh foam has a bright core that breaks at its edge into a reticulated lace of thin filaments and bubble rafts with dark water between them; the transition from foam to water is a translucent greenish tail, not a cut; orion-eft1-floating.jpg: a bright, ragged lapping ring hugs the hull at the waterline.
findings.likelyCause: Hand-off 14 item 1: the foam density is thresholded through the lace texture with a pixel-wide edge, which gives binary coverage, but the inside of the mask is shaded with one albedo and the wave's normal (foam 'has no normal of its own'), and residual foam is the same lace at lower density rather than a thinner, translucent layer; so the result is a flat fill with a hard outline.
findings.fixDirection: Shade foam as a layer: an albedo and opacity that grow with density (thin lace about 0.3 albedo and partly transparent so the water shows through, thick fresh foam about 0.85), a bubble normal map at 2-5 cm with its own small specular sparkle, a soft dark rim of wet water around thick foam, and multi-octave holes inside large patches (the essex photo). Give the hull a lapping foam/meniscus ring driven by the relative heave at the waterline. Judge shoreAlong and splash-1440p at 3x zoom against rough-sea-nato.jpg.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\ocean\splash-1440p.png (reflection column native 820-970 x 710-1020, with black single-pixel specks at native 910-970 x 710-740; hull foot native 787-973 x 698-717), C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\ocean\splash.png (390-500 x 360-510), C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\ocean\perf-splash-1440p.png
findings.defect: The capsule's reflection is a column of per-pixel white salt noise: in the 1440p frame the reflection region has a mean horizontal pixel-to-pixel luma change of 19 against 3.7 in plain water at the same range, i.e. independent pixels, not wobbling horizontal dashes. In motion this will fizz. The hull meets the water along a clean line with no lapping ring, no meniscus, no dark wet band and no darkening of the water right at its foot, and there is no aqua glow of the submerged part.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/sea-surface-close/dragon-crs1-splashdown.jpg and orion-eft1-floating.jpg: the reflection of a floating object is a smeared, vertically stretched image broken into short horizontal bands that follow the wave facets, darker than the object, with coherent shapes over several pixels; a white lapping ring and a darker wet band mark the waterline.
findings.likelyCause: Hand-off 14 item 4: the 12-step reflection march is jittered per pixel by the unresolved slopes; with the screenshot taken from a converged-but-static frame, the jitter is left as noise instead of being integrated into a smooth smear. The waterline contact is not modelled in the ocean's forward pass; the wet band is the vehicle package's.
findings.fixDirection: Jitter the march per sea-anchored facet cell (coherent over a few pixels and stretched across the view direction) rather than per pixel, or blur the hit colour by the unresolved-slope lobe width; keep TAA reactive low on reflections so they are integrated. Add a waterline term in the ocean's pass from 'ocean.wetness' (a thin, slightly darker, foamy contact band where the hull intersects the surface). Ask the vehicle package for the wet band on the real capsule material and re-shoot splash with the real capsule.

findings.defect: Seen from 120-500 m, whitecaps are compact round white lumps 2-4 m across with an aspect ratio near 1.3:1, uniformly white and shaded like pebbles or small ice chunks; none is a crescent across the wind, none trails a streak or a fading patch. Beyond them the 7 m/s sea shows no 'white horses' toward the horizon in any near-surface view (midday, splash, splash-1440p), so the sea reads calmer than its wind.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/sea-surface-close/rough-sea-nato.jpg (elongated streaks 4-8:1 with hard bright cores and translucent tails), beaufort-6.jpg (short bright patches with a sharp leading edge, scattered to the horizon), heavy-seas-essex-1960.jpg (fresh foam bright, old foam a lace, streaks downwind).
findings.likelyCause: Hand-off 14.1: the breaking criterion's excursions are compact, so patches are round; the trail is short (2.4 s) and the foam has no shape of its own along the crest.
findings.fixDirection: As hand-off 14.1 says: low-pass the convergence along the crest only so whole crest segments fire as strips across the wind, advect and stretch the residual downwind for 5-10 s with a lace decay, and render the active crest with a sharp leading edge and a softer trailing tail. Add a spec on patch aspect ratio (median above 3:1 from 150 m).

findings.defect: From LEO the glint is a soft grey disc carrying an even, wallpaper-like spread of marbled contour squiggles, all of similar size and orientation, plus soft dark blots outside the core; the core is neutral grey (179,178,183) rather than warm silver. It reads as marbled paper or frosted plastic. alt100k is a clear improvement and holds up at a glance.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/earth-orbit-ocean/glint-pacific-cb-shadows.jpg, glint-clouds-south-america.jpg, florida-bahamas-glint.jpg: a warm white core (209,184,145), mottled at cloud-shadow and current scales, with a few strong features (fronts, wakes, eddies) and large calm areas; the texture density varies strongly across the disc.
findings.likelyCause: The same slick and gust families as the 3-30 km finding, evaluated with equal density everywhere and seen at a scale where their zero-set contours tile the disc; the neutral colour suggests the lab sky's transmittance at nadir is not reddening the beam the way the real atmosphere does at the ISS's oblique glint angles.
findings.fixDirection: Vary the density of slick features by an order of magnitude across 100-500 km regions (most sea plain, a few active zones), make the features coherent (fronts, eddies, wakes) rather than an even contour texture, and re-check colour and contrast under the integrated atmosphere from LEO.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\ocean\refraction.png (ball 598-670 x 285-308; navy blob 598-630 x 295-308; shallows 0-1280 x 520-720), C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\ocean\handover-refraction.png (ball and blob 595-670 x 255-280; surface speckle 500-900 x 380-560), C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\ocean\shoreAlong.png (700-1280 x 450-720)
findings.defect: Shallow clear water still looks like tinted paint over a blurred bottom. The bed shows only a soft, low-contrast bokeh mottle; there is no sharp caustic net, no readable sand ripples. The submerged ball's image is a flat saucer with a crisp outline, and a hard-edged navy blob (median (30,61,75) against turquoise) sits beside and below it, still reading as a hole or a decal. In handover-refraction the whole mid-field surface carries per-pixel cyan speckle (mean |dx| 11.2 against 2.9 in shoreAlong's shallows) that will shimmer in motion.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/earth-orbit-ocean/bahamas-shallows.jpg (bottom colour through a few metres of water with sharp, sinuous 1.5-2x brightness edges); reentry-chutes/artemis2-underwater-heatshield.jpg (an object through water: blue-cyan cast, soft fall-off, no cut-out). Any sunlit sandy shallow: a bright, sharp, moving caustic net, the object tinted green-yellow with a wobbling broken outline and no dark patch beside it.
findings.likelyCause: Hand-off 14.1: caustics are 1/|det(1 + aH)| from cascades 2-3 at their texel size, so the net is low-pass; the navy blob is the bed in the ball's shadow seen unrefracted where the refraction march is not trusted; the speckle looks like the bed texture or caustic term point-sampled through the refraction offset without footprint filtering.
findings.fixDirection: Add a dedicated caustics texture (projected along the refracted sun, 2-4 cm texels, two scrolling octaves) clamped and faded with depth; where the refraction march is not trusted, blend to the bed beside the object (as for the depth) instead of showing the shadowed bed unrefracted; filter the bed/caustic lookup by the refracted footprint so no per-pixel speckle survives. Spec: colour inside the ball's unrefracted silhouette within a few percent of the water around it after TAA has converged.

findings.defect: The surf is a constant-width double outline: from 60 m one white swash line on the sand and one breaker line a few metres out, parallel to the beach along its whole length, with no surf zone between them; from water level (shore, shore-1440p) the beach is reached by a teal sea with only a faint white thread at the waterline and no breaking wave silhouettes. No wet sand behind the swash.
findings.realReference: Aerial and beach photographs of a sandy shore with 1-2 m swell: a white surf zone tens of metres wide, several irregular breaker lines that start and stop along the beach, bores that run up as lacy sheets and leave a dark glossy wet band; from water level the breakers rise as bright crests in front of the beach.
findings.likelyCause: Hand-off 14 item 11: bores are spawned where the bed is shallower than 2.2 m from the swell phase, which on the lab's steep beach is a narrow strip of constant width; the run-up is drawn as foam only; wet sand needs a contract entry and the terrain.
findings.fixDirection: Scale the breaking zone with the shelf slope and swell height (break where depth < 0.8-1.3 Hs, which on a gentle shelf is tens of metres), vary the breaker lines along the beach with the swell's directional phase so they start and stop, draw the breaking crest as a raised white line visible from water level, and file the contract request for a shore-wetness band so the terrain can darken the run-up zone.

findings.defect: From 2-3 m the sea still reads as a flat textured sheet: the horizon is a ruled line, no crest rises to hide the trough behind it or the foot of the capsule, and the foreground is covered in soft-edged dark navy blotches (like camouflage or cloud shadows) under a uniform fine ripple; under overcast the foreground is a crumpled-foil texture with no wave forms. For the stated 7 m/s wind with Hs about 1.7 m this is a Beaufort 2 look.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/sea-surface-close/orion-eft1-floating.jpg and apollo9-floats.jpg: short-crested wind waves with distinct dark faces and bright backs at metre scale, crests that partly hide the water and the hull beyond them, a slightly ragged horizon from a boat, and a few white horses toward the horizon.
findings.likelyCause: The drawn heights are the physics swell (eight long plane waves, steepness at most 0.0175, render-only heights declined by the lead, hand-off 14.1); the short-crested wind sea exists only as normals (long-wave layer, far bank), so it has no parallax or occlusion, and the long-wave layer's slopes at metre scale print as soft blotches rather than wave faces.
findings.fixDirection: With the lead: either physics data with a short-crested wind sea of realistic steepness (0.03-0.05 around 40-70 m), or permission for render-only heights faded to the physics surface within a few hull radii of any vessel. In the ocean's paths: shape the long-wave layer's normals into crest-aligned faces (sharpened crests, Gerstner-like horizontal displacement in the normal derivation) so the foreground shows wave faces instead of blotches.

findings.defect: The far field carries isolated, uniformly sized 2x2 white specks spread evenly toward the horizon, all of similar brightness, like dust or stuck pixels.
findings.realReference: Photographs with the sun ahead at moderate elevation: distant glints are clustered on wave crests and vary in size and brightness; they twinkle and form short dashes across the view.
findings.likelyCause: Not verified: glitter draws (or the statistical whitecap share) at the far field emitted as single pixels with a fixed size and no clustering by wave phase.
findings.fixDirection: Modulate the far glitter by the resolved wave phase so sparkles cluster on crests, vary their intensity with the Poisson count, and stretch them horizontally at grazing angles.

findings.defect: Under a clear sky the sea is a milky grey-lavender: mid-field (119,142,171), near the horizon (136,154,175), under a nearly white horizon sky (210,214,212). The Fresnel ramp itself is right (sea under the horizon 0.47x the sky, near water 0.16x), but the colour lacks the saturated cobalt of a clear-day sea.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/sea-surface-close/artemis2-floating-2.jpg: sky above the horizon (163,201,238), sea under it (89,137,191) at 0.45x, near sea (40,77,116).
findings.likelyCause: The lab sky's horizon is too white and desaturated (lab-only, not the ocean's), so the mirrored sky is grey.
findings.fixDirection: Re-judge the near-surface views under the integrated atmosphere; if the lab is to stay the reference, give its sky a bluer, less hazy horizon so the water can be judged against photographs.

findings.defect: Near the horizon the far sea shows large smooth curved dark swoops and fan-like lines converging on the vanishing point, like a sheet of silk, rather than compressed horizontal bands.
findings.realReference: Any photograph of the open sea from tens of metres: the far water compresses into fine horizontal streaks that brighten toward the horizon; wave envelopes are not visible as smooth curves.
findings.likelyCause: Far-wave bank components with their own envelopes and bent crests (hand-off 14 item 3) seen at grazing angles, where each envelope becomes a long smooth curve.
findings.fixDirection: Shorten the envelopes and increase the component count at grazing footprints, or fade the bank's envelope modulation as the footprint's anisotropy grows.

findings.defect: For this review the functional project was re-run through the gate (15:06-15:20 on 2026-11-11, 32 of 32 passed), so every functional screenshot is current. The three perf screenshots are still from 14:43-14:44, before the last ocean source commit (01ceeb9, 14:46), and every integrated-app water view is from 11:09-11:21, before round 1 started. The hand-off's claim that the haze from 10 km up is the atmosphere's rests on views of the old water.
findings.realReference: A reviewed screenshot set from the current build: the native-resolution and integrated views re-shot after the last source change.

Anything that is not a vessel slot (marker floats, a pier, the pad's towers seen across the lagoon, the beach's own edge) will float above the water without a mirror image.
findings.realReference: out/qa/ref/launch-pad/lc39a-aerial.jpg (lagoon water mirrors the sky and structures), liftoff-ascent/sts97-smoke-steam-night.jpg (the plume reflected in the water as bright as the plume): calm water mirrors every object near it.
findings.likelyCause: Hand-off 14 item 4: the reflection march runs only for rays that pass near a vessel's hull (the perf cut that brought splashdown p50 from 1.04 to 0.87 ms).
findings.fixDirection: Keep the vessel march, and add a cheap screen-space reflection fallback for all opaque geometry in the colour/depth copies at grazing reflected rays (a few steps, blurred by the lobe), faded where it misses; or state the limitation and keep objects that matter (pad, recovery ships, chutes on the water) registered as reflection slots.
